Who We Are
:

Mental Health Support Services (MHSS) is the provider of mental health, developmental disabilities, and substance use disorder services for children and adults in Chesterfield County. The Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) team is seeking a qualified and experienced Case Manager to join our dynamic, interdisciplinary team that provides intensive, community-based services to individuals with serious mental illness diagnoses.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in a human services field, such as psychology, sociology, rehabilitation counseling, or a related field; two years of experience in a human services field; or an equivalent combination of training and experience. Two years of experience working with individuals with mental illness preferred; experience with benefits navigation, Department of Social Services/Social Security Administration systems, or case management preferred. Qualified Mental Health Professional certification preferred; experience working for a Community Services Board (CSB) preferred; experience with an electronic health record preferred.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Working knowledge of case management methods, practices, and procedures. Ability to interview clients to identify deficiencies in personal, social, economic and health needs; to work in a multi-disciplinary team environment providing treatment and rehabilitation services; to communicate effectively orally and in writing; to operate a personal computer and related software and other standard office equipment; to develop and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external customers. Knowledge of mental illness, community resources, Medicaid benefits, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), housing resources, and local support systems preferred. Strong organizational and time management skills for tracking deadlines, benefits cycles, and documentation requirements preferred. Ability to work effectively with clients experiencing homelessness, acute mental health symptoms, co-occurring disorders, or limited engagement preferred. Ability to collaborate in a high intensity ACT environment preferred.

Additional Requirements

Current valid driver’s license and good driving record required. Based on the Virginia DMV point system, records must not reflect a total of six or more demerit points within the twenty-four months preceding the anticipated hire date, or one major violation of six demerit points within the preceding thirty-six months. Out-of-state driving records must be
obtained by applicant and presented at time of interview. Records must reflect at least three years of history and be dated within thirty days of interview date.

Pre-employment drug testing, FBI criminal background check and education/degree verification required.

Duties

Duties Include But Are Not Limited To The Following

Provides care coordination and assists individuals with serious mental illness to navigate benefits systems (SNAP, energy/cooling assistance, Social Security) and access community supports;
Links clients to community resources including primary care, housing supports, dental/vision care, transportation, financial programs, and other community services;
Tracks and monitors referrals and follow-ups;
Facilitates care coordination and follows up with external providers;
Works collaboratively with the multidisciplinary ACT Team to support client stability and recovery;
Actively participates in daily ACT team meetings to share updates, plan outreach, and coordinate services;
Documents all client contacts according to Medicaid, Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services (DBHDS), Community Service Board (CSB), and ACT Team requirements;
Completes annual required paperwork with clients; and
Performs other work as required.

This position is a part of an approved Career Development Plan (CDP) and offers career progression opportunities and salary incentives, as funding permits, based on performance, qualifications, and experience.

Company Overview

Lotus Neuro is a clinical-stage therapeutics development company pioneering a novel approach to treating the most intractable diseases of the brain. The company leverages a proven and proprietary low-frequency focused ultrasound technology to open the blood–brain barrier non-invasively and transiently, which, in combination with advanced therapeutics, unlocks an entirely new pathway for treating complex brain diseases. To date, the platform has been used in approximately 600 therapeutic cycles across indications including brain tumors, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and ALS.

Lotus Neuro was launched in December 2025 as a spinout of Insightec, a global medical technology company focused on realizing the therapeutic power of acoustic energy. Lotus Neuro raised $50M in seed financing, backed by a Strategic Foundation Investor, a leading investment firm dedicated to advancing the treatment and management of brain disorders.

We are a small, fast-moving team. Clarity, accountability, and disciplined execution matter here — every person's work visibly moves the company forward.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Program Manager to keep our programs organized, aligned, on schedule, and moving. You will be the connective tissue across our preclinical, regulatory, clinical, and partnership workstreams — turning company goals and meeting decisions into tracked, completed work.

This is a hands-on role for someone who thrives on bringing order to a complex, multi-stakeholder environment. You will help drive the company's top goals, own milestones and timelines, support key governance and working-group meetings, coordinate external partners and vendors, and keep our operating system accurate and useful.

Key Responsibilities

Corporate Strategic Operations

Help align and drive the company's annual goals — breaking them into milestones, owners, and timelines, and keeping cross-functional stakeholders aligned and accountable to plan.
Maintain and update the company-wide integrated schedule, tracking milestones, dependencies, and timelines across preclinical, regulatory, clinical, and partnership workstreams.
Translate decisions and action items from leadership and recurring meetings into clear, assigned, time-bound tasks — and follow up to ensure they are completed.
Maintain the company's project and operations data in Monday.com, keeping goals, milestones, and action-item boards current and reliable.
Produce simple, clear status updates so leadership always knows where each effort stands.
Flag risks, delays, and bottlenecks early, and help drive them to resolution.

External Stakeholder Management

Manage joint committees and working-group meetings with our partners — building agendas, capturing decisions and action items, and driving follow-through to closure.
Manage interactions with the network of clinical sites, tracking status and driving actions.
Help coordinate clinical site outreach, program logistics, and partner engagements.

Preclinical & Vendor Coordination

Manage preclinical studies, coordinating the network of CROs, vendors, and labs to align deliverables, data, and timelines.
Manage other vendors, CROs, and contracts — tracking scope, deliverables, and status through execution.
Support preparation for regulatory milestones by tracking deliverables and helping in assembling materials on schedule.

Documentation & Information Management

Organize and maintain shared files, partner data rooms, and document repositories so the right people can find the right materials quickly.
Track the status of contracts and agreements through execution, coordinating with internal and external stakeholders to keep them moving.
Support meeting planning and travel logistics for site visits, partner engagements, and conferences / scientific advisory boards as needed.

Who We're Looking For

Required

At least 5 years of program or project management experience, ideally in biotech, pharma, medical device, or a CRO / life-sciences setting.
Excellent people skills and a track record of driving company goals and complex, multi-stakeholder programs to completion — owning milestones, timelines, and follow-through in a fast-paced environment.
Strong meeting-management skills: building agendas, capturing decisions and actions, and holding owners accountable.
Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills, with strong attention to detail and reliable follow-through.
Hands-on proficiency with project-management and collaboration tools (e.g., Monday.com, Smartsheet) and standard office / productivity software.
Comfort working autonomously in a small-team setting while taking direction from leadership.

Preferred

Familiarity with the drug-development and / or clinical-trial lifecycle and common terminology (preclinical studies, IND / regulatory milestones, clinical operations).
Experience coordinating CROs, labs, or other external scientific / clinical vendors, and managing contracts through execution.
Experience running partner or joint governance meetings.
Exposure to EOS / Traction or a comparable operating system.
PMP, CAPM, or equivalent project / program-management certification.

Why Join Us

You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with an experienced leadership team on technology with the potential to change how brain diseases are treated. Your work will directly accelerate our path to the clinic — and you'll have the visibility, ownership, and impact that only an early-stage company can offer.

Core Values

It is critical that the Program Manager embraces and promotes Lotus Neuro's core values:

Lead with Love. We lead with humility, integrity of intent, and a commitment to elevate others.
Own the Challenge. We take responsibility, pursue excellence, and solve problems proactively.
Thrive through Failure. We learn fast, speak openly, and move forward stronger through adversity.

Location and Working Model

Lotus Neuro operates as a virtual company with Miami, FL as its corporate home. The Program Manager may travel to Boston, Miami, CRO sites, and the Lotus Neuro clinical site network in the United States and abroad.

Amazon Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) Operational Excellence (OpEx) is seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead execution of safety performance improvement programs targeting the network's highest-opportunity sites. This role owns the operational cadence for a portfolio of enrolled sites, translating data-driven insights into site-level interventions that produce measurable, sustained injury rate reduction. The ideal candidate combines deep program management experience with analytical rigor and a bias for action in complex, cross-functional environments.

You will operate as a force multiplier for a Principal Program Manager, independently managing day-to-day program operations across a growing enrollment base while partnering with business unit leaders, data science teams, and field WHS professionals to drive execution. This role requires comfort with ambiguity, the ability to influence without authority across multiple organizations, and a track record of improving safety mechanisms on site. Some travel required (roughly 25%, up to 50%).

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end execution cadence for program-enrolled sites, including quarterly reviews, site improvement plan tracking, graduation criteria monitoring, and escalation management. Partner with business intelligence and data science teams to build reporting mechanisms, validate intervention effectiveness, and surface actionable performance insights to business unit leaders. Analyze site-level performance data to identify emerging risks, monitor progress against improvement plans, and inform resource allocation decisions. Coordinate with business unit points of contact across multiple organizations to ensure consistent execution, remove barriers, and drive accountability from site to regional leadership. Support program scaling initiatives including new enrollment cycles, tiered support model expansion, and integration of additional business units and geographies. Drive continuous improvement of program processes, playbooks, and templates to enable standardized execution as enrollment grows. Conduct site visits alongside business unit partners to assess implementation quality, validate corrective actions, and identify cross-site best practices for replication. Support preparation of program-level reporting and communications to senior leadership, including monthly flash reports, VP-level updates, and executive reviews.

A day in the life

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include: 1. Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage 2. Maternity and Parental Leave Options 3. Paid Time Off (PTO) 4. 401(k) Plan

Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) Operational Excellence (OpEx) is committed to the continual improvement of people, processes, and performance to position Amazon as an industry leader in safety excellence. OpEx partners with cross-functional teams to resolve global challenges and support 8,000+ WHS professionals. We leverage data, causal analysis, and structured intervention models to identify performance risks and drive measurable safety outcomes at scale. We are open to hiring candidates to work from the following locations: Nashville, Bellevue, Kansas City, or Arlington.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Bachelor's degree
Experience leading cross-functional projects and managing stakeholders across multiple organizations

Preferred Qualifications

5+ years driving process improvements in operations, safety, or continuous improvement environments
5+ years managing stakeholders in cross-functional project delivery
Experience with site-level performance improvement programs or multi-site operational excellence initiatives
Familiarity with safety metrics (RIR, LTIR, SIR) and intervention effectiveness analysis

Description

Amazon Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) Operational Excellence (OpEx) is seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead execution of safety performance improvement programs targeting the network's highest-opportunity sites. This role owns the operational cadence for a portfolio of enrolled sites, translating data-driven insights into site-level interventions that produce measurable, sustained injury rate reduction. The ideal candidate combines deep program management experience with analytical rigor and a bias for action in complex, cross-functional environments.

You will operate as a force multiplier for a Principal Program Manager, independently managing day-to-day program operations across a growing enrollment base while partnering with business unit leaders, data science teams, and field WHS professionals to drive execution. This role requires comfort with ambiguity, the ability to influence without authority across multiple organizations, and a track record of improving safety mechanisms on site. Some travel required (roughly 25%, up to 50%).

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end execution cadence for program-enrolled sites, including quarterly reviews, site improvement plan tracking, graduation criteria monitoring, and escalation management. Partner with business intelligence and data science teams to build reporting mechanisms, validate intervention effectiveness, and surface actionable performance insights to business unit leaders. Analyze site-level performance data to identify emerging risks, monitor progress against improvement plans, and inform resource allocation decisions. Coordinate with business unit points of contact across multiple organizations to ensure consistent execution, remove barriers, and drive accountability from site to regional leadership. Support program scaling initiatives including new enrollment cycles, tiered support model expansion, and integration of additional business units and geographies. Drive continuous improvement of program processes, playbooks, and templates to enable standardized execution as enrollment grows. Conduct site visits alongside business unit partners to assess implementation quality, validate corrective actions, and identify cross-site best practices for replication. Support preparation of program-level reporting and communications to senior leadership, including monthly flash reports, VP-level updates, and executive reviews.

A day in the life

new_jobs.description:
Position Description & Qualifications

Are you passionate about health and fitness and ready to make a significant impact in the lives of those who serve our country? Come be a part of the US Army’s groundbreaking Holistic Health and Fitness (H2F) program. H2F is dedicated to improving not just the physical fitness, but the overall well-being of soldiers at all levels.

Serco is seeking an Alternate Program Manager to support the Holistic Health and Fitness (H2F) program.

The Holistic Health and Fitness (H2F) initiative is the Army’s investment in Soldier Readiness. The H2F Alternate Program Manager (APM) reports to the Program Manager (PM) and together with the PM is responsible for the contract’s overall performance, achieving performance standards, workforce management, customer satisfaction, contract compliance, and quality control. As such, the H2F Alternate Program Manager shall have full authority to act for Serco Inc. on all contract matters relating to this contract’s daily operation during the absence of the PM. This position requires access to U.S. Government facilities and systems.

In This Role, You Will

Be available Monday-Friday, 0800-1700 Eastern Time.
Be responsible for the overall performance of work, compliance, and quality control.
Be responsible for plans, strategies, employee management, and monitoring and controlling activities to effectively support the Army H2F program and stakeholders at all locations.
Serve as the primary customer point of contact with the COR, U.S. Army Transformation and Training Command (T2COM) leadership, and Army installation stakeholders in the absence of the PM.
Develop strategies for specialized H2F recruiting, credentialing, retention, and employee well-being initiatives and maintain, update, and monitor their effectiveness.
Oversee and direct recruitment and screening process to ensure all certifications and credentials are valid, current, and fulfill customer requirements before onboarding.
Establish and maintain an effective quality control program.
Generate and submit a Task Order Status Report (TOSR) through the Human Resource Solutions portal each month and other deliverables in the Performance Requirements Summary.
Provide direction to subcontractor points of contact and effective oversight of subcontractor workforce.

Please visit our landing page for more information:
U.S. Army Holistic Health & Fitness (H2F) System (serco.com)

Visit the following link for more information about how Serco supports our Veterans
https://www.serco.com/na/careers/veterans-at-serco

To Be Successful In This Role, You Will Have

U.S. Citizenship.
The ability to pass and maintain a NACI (Tier 1) to obtain access to U.S. Government facilities and systems.
A master’s degree from an accredited university or college in business, management, or operations and/or another master's degree relevant to the profession/program such as exercise science or kinesiology.
Five (5) years of experience managing, staffing, overseeing, and completing large government projects of geographically dispersed locations (250 plus personnel) related to the above job description.
Five (5) years of experience working with a military or DoD organization(s) related to the job description above.
A valid driver's license, transportation, and auto insurance.
The ability to travel up to 25% of the time, as required.

Additional Desired Experience And Skills

Active NACI.
Project Management Professional Certification.
Experience with government contracting.
National Strength and Conditioning Association Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS) or Collegiate Strength and Conditioning Coaches Association Strength and Conditioning Coach Certified (SCCC).
In-depth understanding of US Army culture, lifestyle, and command structures.
Military leadership experience.
Educational or professional background in exercise science, health science, physical education, human performance, kinesiology, sports sciences, and/or sports psychology.
Articulates understanding of basic evaluation techniques and use of customer feedback to improve overall program effectiveness/impact.
Demonstrates the ability to manage multiple priorities, illustrates attention to detail, and shows evidence of being conscientious regarding deadlines.
Ability to work in a collaborative environment with remotely located team members.

If you are interested in supporting and working with our U.S. Military and a passionate Serco team, submit your application now for immediate consideration. It only takes a few minutes and could change your career!

Military Veterans and Spouses are encouraged to apply!
